explain.say: Twins are two babies who develop at the same time. There are two quite different ways it can happen, and they lead to identical or non-identical twins.

explain.say: Identical twins come from one fertilised egg that splits into two embryos in the first days. They share almost exactly the same DNA, so they are always the same sex and look extremely alike.

explain.say: Non-identical twins come from two separate eggs, each fertilised separately. They share about half their gene versions, like any brother and sister, and can be a boy and a girl.

explain.say: Even identical twins are not perfect copies. Their fingerprints differ, and small changes in how genes are switched on, plus different life experiences, make them more different as they grow.

faq.a: Identical twins form when a single fertilised egg splits into two separate embryos, usually within about two weeks. Because they came from one cell, they share nearly the same DNA.
asks: Do identical twins come from one egg?

faq.a: Non-identical, or fraternal, twins form when two eggs are released at the same time and each is fertilised. They are genetically as similar as ordinary brothers and sisters.
asks: Can twins be a boy and a girl?

faq.q: Do identical twins have the same fingerprints?
faq.a: No. Fingerprints form before birth as the skin grows and buckles, and tiny differences in position and pressure in the womb make every fingerprint unique, even in identical twins.
asks: Can identical twins be told apart by fingerprints?

faq.a: Non-identical twins can run in families, because some women tend to release more than one egg at a time. Identical twins happen at about the same rate everywhere and are thought to be largely random.
asks: Why do some families have lots of twins?

faq.q: Why do identical twins become more different with age?
faq.a: Even with the same DNA, different food, activities and experiences change their bodies, and chemical tags that switch genes on and off build up differently over the years.
asks: Are identical twins exactly the same?
Why do twins look different when older?

facts: Identical twins occur in about 3 to 4 of every 1,000 births worldwide.
The rate of non-identical twins varies between countries and tends to run in families.

quiz.say: Twins are a boy and a girl. What kind of twins must they be?
quiz.show: Boy and girl twins must be…
quiz.why: Identical twins come from one fertilised egg and so are the same sex; boy-girl twins came from two eggs.

wrong.0: Identical twins share almost the same DNA, including the sex chromosomes.
wrong.2: Only non-identical twins can be a boy and a girl.
